subject: URGENT: Opal Health - retry wave causing 5xx/429 spike
body:
--- Message 1/4 ---
From: Amira Khanna <amira.k@opalhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-11T09:42:01Z
Subject: High error rate & timeouts in production - multiple customers impacted

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a big uptick in 5xx and 429 responses to our production calls around 09:10 UTC this morning. Several downstream RT endpoints are timing out (30s) and our frontend shows repeated retries from users.

Impact: two paying customers reported session failures and follow-up support tickets; we had to roll back a small release but the errors persist.

Attached are a short sample of failing request traces (opal-error-samples.log) and timestamps showing the error spike. Can your team confirm whether this is throttling, autoscale lag, or something else? Conversation is heating up here and we need ETA on fix and an interim mitigation we can apply on our side.

Amira
Head of Platform Ops
Opal Health

---

--- Message 2/4 ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Khanna <amira.k@opalhealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-11T10:05:12Z
Subject: Re: High error rate & timeouts in production - multiple customers impacted

Amira — thank you for the samples. I’ve looped in Lauren and Markus from Ops to triage immediately. Initial ask: can you confirm whether these requests were routed to your Dedicated pool or to our hosted fallback?

We’re treating this as high priority; I’ll provide an update in 15–20 minutes with metrics and a recommended short-term mitigation. If we need to, we’ll escalate to exec attention for credits/SLA exceptions.

Short note for Opal: until we have a fix, you can temporarily reduce max-concurrency on the client side (example: requests/sec -> 50% of current) and enable exponential backoff to avoid amplifying retries — we’ll try to avoid asking you to change client behavior if possible.

— Marissa

--- Message 3/4 ---
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc:
Date: 2026-12-11T10:22:34Z
Subject: Re: High error rate & timeouts in production - multiple customers impacted

Quick findings from the Dedicated pool metrics (attaching a snapshot):
- Around 09:08–09:12 UTC we observed a burst of long-context requests (avg seq_len ~12k tokens) from a small subset of Opal API keys.
- The Dedicated GPU pool reached sustained >98% utilization and the autoscaler attempted to spin up additional nodes but provisioning laged ~4m due to spot allocation churn in the region. This produced a short window of queueing where requests tripped our 5xx path and clients retried.
- Retry amplification likely caused the secondary 429s; client retries hit the queued endpoints while backend was trying to provision.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Temporarily raised priority on Opal's Reserved pool and routed non-latency-critical traffic to a cold-hosted fallback cluster (model downgraded to a smaller variant to preserve cost).
2) Blacklisted the abnormal long-context pattern as a short-term mitigation to prevent pipeline clogging.
3) Opened SUP-3321 to track the autoscale provisioning failure and to add a fast-warm path for critical reserved pools.

Attachments: pool-metrics-20261211.png

Next: Markus is validating log-level traces for failed tokens and I’ll coordinate a postmortem once we confirm root cause and timeline for autoscaler fix.

— Lauren
Ops Lead — Serving Runtime
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

--- Message 4/4 ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, Amira Khanna <amira.k@opalhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T08:15:00Z
Subject: URGENT: Opal Health - retry storm + 5xx spike (exec attention)

Karthik — raising this to you for visibility and quick decision on customer remediation. TL;DR: Opal (Reserved Dedicated pool) experienced a provisioning lag during a burst of very long-context requests, which led to GPU exhaustion, request queueing, and a retry amplification wave resulting in 5xx/429 spikes.

What we’ve done so far:
- Short-term routing to hosted fallback with a smaller model to keep Opal traffic flowing
- Blacklisted the client pattern that created extremely long sequences
- Created SUP-3321 to fix autoscale warm-path and improve provisioning SLOs

Impact & ask from leadership:
- Opal has two paying customers impacted and is asking for credits and an SLA exception for the incident window (09:08–09:25 UTC).
- Recommend we approve a goodwill credit (one month proration) and prioritize the autoscaler hot-warm path engineering ticket in the next sprint.
- Suggest a joint postmortem with Opal; I can own the external recap and remediation plan.

Proposed mitigation timeline:
- Short-term (today): continue hosted fallback + client-side backoff guidance (implemented)
- Near-term (72 hours): rollout autoscaler fast-warm patch to staging and limited production pilot for Reserved pools
- Longer-term (2–4 weeks): increase pool warm capacity options and add runbook for immediate manual warm-up during spikes

Amira — we’ll keep you updated and can schedule a 30-min sync today to walk through the remediation plan and credits proposal.

Marissa
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
